headline: When a Pipe Bursts: What to Do First
articleBody: Suddenly finding yourself with a burst pipe can be incredibly stressful, but knowing what to do immediately can significantly reduce damage. The key is to act fast and keep calm. First, locate your main water shutoff valve and turn it off completely. This stops the flow of water and prevents further flooding. If you can’t find the main valve, or if it's too difficult to reach, try to shut off the isolation valve for the specific fixture that's leaking, if there is one. Once the water is off, open a few cold water taps and flush toilets to help relieve any pressure in the system. This can minimize additional drips or sprays. Move any valuables or furniture away from the affected area if it's safe to do so. Documentation is also helpful; take pictures of the damage before and after you've taken initial steps. Trying to make complex repairs yourself in a panic is usually a bad idea. These kinds of situations require a professional, especially if the source of the leak is hidden or near electrical components.
